# Full-Stack Blog CMS with TanStack Start (SSR + Server Functions + SQLite)

## Background

Build a full-stack, server-side-rendered blog content management system using TanStack Start (React, file-based routing, and server functions) backed by a local SQLite database. A TanStack Start project has already been scaffolded for you at the project path below; you must implement the application on top of it.

## Requirements

* Full CRUD for blog posts: create, edit, delete, and list.
* Every post has these fields: `title`, `slug` (auto-generated and unique), `body` (authored in Markdown), `tags` (zero or more), and a published/draft status.
* The public post detail page MUST be server-side rendered: the post's title and its rendered body MUST be present in the initial HTML document returned by the server (i.e. visible without executing any client-side JavaScript) so the page is indexable for SEO.
* A post's `body` is written in Markdown and MUST be rendered to HTML when the post is viewed.
* The public post list MUST show only published posts. Draft posts MUST never be reachable or visible through any public page.
* An admin post list MUST show all posts, including drafts.
* The public post list MUST be filterable by tag through the URL.
* Requesting a post that does not exist (or that is a draft) through a public URL MUST return a 404 not-found page.
* All data MUST be persisted in a local SQLite database and MUST survive a full restart of the server.

## Implementation Hints

* Project path: /home/user/blog
* The application MUST run as a production, server-side-rendered build and be served on port 43117, reachable at http://localhost:43117.
  * Build command: `npm run build`
  * Start command: `PORT=43117 npm run start`
* Exact routes and their required behavior:
  * `GET /` — public list of published posts only. Each listed post's title MUST be an anchor (`<a>`) element whose `href` is exactly `/posts/<slug>`. When the query parameter `tag` is present (e.g. `/?tag=<tag>`), the list MUST show only published posts that have that exact tag.
  * `GET /posts/<slug>` — public detail page for a single published post. The post title MUST be rendered inside an `<h1>` element. The Markdown body, rendered to HTML, MUST be placed inside an element carrying the attribute `data-testid="post-body"`. The title and the rendered body text MUST appear in the raw server-rendered HTML of this route. If `<slug>` does not correspond to an existing published post, the server MUST respond with HTTP status code 404 and render a page whose visible text contains `Not Found`.
  * `GET /admin` — admin list of ALL posts (both published and draft). Each post's title MUST appear as text on this page. For each post the page MUST provide a delete control implemented as a `<button>` element carrying the attribute `data-testid="delete-<slug>"` that permanently deletes that post.
  * `GET /admin/new` — a form to create a new post.
  * `GET /admin/<slug>/edit` — a form to edit the post with that slug, pre-filled with the post's current values.
* The create form and the edit form MUST both contain these controls:
  * a text input with attribute `name="title"`
  * a textarea with attribute `name="body"`
  * a text input with attribute `name="tags"` that accepts a comma-separated list of tags
  * a checkbox with attribute `name="published"` (checked means published, unchecked means draft)
  * a control that submits and saves the post
* Tag parsing: the value of the `tags` field is split on commas and each entry is trimmed of surrounding whitespace; empty entries are ignored. Tag filtering matches a tag string exactly.
* Slug generation: derive the slug from the title by lowercasing it, replacing every run of characters outside the set `[a-z0-9]` with a single `-`, and trimming any leading or trailing `-`. If the resulting slug is already used by another post, append `-N`, using the smallest integer N greater than or equal to 2 that makes the slug unique (for example `my-title`, then `my-title-2`, then `my-title-3`).
* Markdown rendering MUST convert standard Markdown to the corresponding HTML elements (for example, `## Section` becomes an `<h2>` and `**bold**` becomes a `<strong>` element).
* Editing a post MUST persist the changes; deleting a post MUST remove it from both the admin and public views.

## Notes

* All services are local. Do NOT use any external API, network service, or third-party hosted service.

Title: Hosting | TanStack Start React Docs

URL Source: https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting

Markdown Content:
Hosting is the process of deploying your application to the internet so that users can access it. This is a critical part of any web development project, ensuring your application is available to the world. TanStack Start supports Vite and Rsbuild, giving you flexible build outputs for different hosting providers and runtimes.

TanStack Start is **designed to work with any hosting provider**, so if you already have a hosting provider in mind, you can deploy your application there using the full-stack APIs provided by TanStack Start.

However, since hosting is one of the most crucial aspects of your application's performance, reliability, and scalability, we recommend using one of our **Official Hosting Partners**: [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/?utm_source=tanstack), [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com/?utm_source=tanstack), or [Railway](https://railway.com/?utm_source=tanstack).

Once you've chosen a deployment target, you can follow the deployment guidelines below to deploy your TanStack Start application to the hosting provider of your choice:

*   [cloudflare-workers](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#cloudflare-workers--official-partner): Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
*   [netlify](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#netlify--official-partner): Deploy to Netlify
*   [railway](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#railway--official-partner): Deploy to Railway
*   [nitro](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#nitro): Deploy using Nitro
*   [vercel](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#vercel): Deploy to Vercel
*   [node-server](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#nodejs--docker): Deploy to a Node.js server
*   [bun](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#bun): Deploy to a Bun server
*   [appwrite-sites](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#appwrite-sites): Deploy to Appwrite Sites
*   ... and more to come!

### Cloudflare Workers ⭐ _Official Partner_

[![Image 1: Cloudflare logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tanstack/tanstack.com/main/src/images/cloudflare-black.svg)](https://www.cloudflare.com/?utm_source=tanstack)

When deploying to Cloudflare Workers, you'll need to complete a few extra steps before your users can start using your app. The official Cloudflare Workers setup currently uses Vite through @cloudflare/vite-plugin.

1.   Install @cloudflare/vite-plugin and wrangler

1.   Add the Cloudflare plugin to your vite.config.ts file

1.   Add a wrangler.jsonc config file

1.   Modify the scripts in your package.json file

1.   Login with Wrangler to authenticate with your Cloudflare account.

or if using pnpm:

To check current user use wrangler whoami.

1.   Deploy

Deploy your application to Cloudflare Workers using their one-click deployment process, and you're ready to go!

A full TanStack Start example for Cloudflare Workers is available [here](https://github.com/TanStack/router/tree/main/examples/react/start-basic-cloudflare).

### Netlify ⭐ _Official Partner_

[![Image 2: Netlify logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tanstack/tanstack.com/main/src/images/netlify-light.svg)](https://www.netlify.com/?utm_source=tanstack)

The official Netlify setup currently uses Vite through [@netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start), which configures your build for Netlify deployment and provides full Netlify production platform emulation in local dev:

Finally, use [Netlify CLI](https://developers.netlify.com/cli/) to deploy your app:

If this is a new Netlify project, you'll be prompted to initialize it and build settings will be automatically configured for you.

For more detailed documentation, check out the full [TanStack Start on Netlify docs](https://docs.netlify.com/build/frameworks/framework-setup-guides/tanstack-start/).

#### Manual configuration

Alternatively, if you prefer manual configuration, you can add a netlify.toml file to your project root:

Or you can set the above settings directly [in the Netlify app](https://docs.netlify.com/build/configure-builds/overview/#build-settings).

#### Other deployment methods

Netlify also supports other deployment methods, such as [continuous deployment from a git repo hosted on GitHub, GitLab, or others](https://docs.netlify.com/start/quickstarts/deploy-from-repository/), [starting from a template](https://docs.netlify.com/start/quickstarts/deploy-from-template/), [deploying or importing from an AI code generation tool](https://docs.netlify.com/start/quickstarts/deploy-from-ai-code-generation-tool/), and [more](https://docs.netlify.com/deploy/create-deploys/).

### Railway ⭐ _Official Partner_

[![Image 3: Railway logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tanstack/tanstack.com/main/src/images/railway-light.svg)](https://railway.com/?utm_source=tanstack)

Railway provides instant deployments with zero configuration. Follow the [Nitro](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting#nitro) deployment instructions, then deploy to Railway:

1.   Push your code to a GitHub repository

2.   Connect your repository to Railway at [railway.com](https://railway.com/?utm_source=tanstack)

3.   Railway will automatically detect your build settings and deploy your application

Railway automatically provides:

*   **Automatic deployments** on every push to your repository
*   **Built-in databases** (Postgres, MySQL, Redis, MongoDB)
*   **Preview environments** for pull requests
*   **Automatic HTTPS** and custom domains

For more details, see [Railway's documentation](https://docs.railway.com/).

### Nitro
